key_insight: SPICE-Q proposes a unified design-technology co-optimization workflow that links superconducting qubit fabrication constraints to electromagnetic simulation, circuit models, quantum dynamics, and yield.
engineering_relevance: It gives quantum hardware teams a traceable, standardized pipeline for improving large-scale chip manufacturability, performance predictability, and feedback-driven process control.
method: Connects process/PDK rules to layout, EM simulation, EPR/circuit quantization, Hamiltonian extraction, and noise analysis
Uses standardized model interfaces, statistical parameter models, model cards, and version governance
Closes the loop with cryogenic test and fabrication data to calibrate models and improve yield
evidence_signal: The abstract describes the framework conceptually and by its toolchain coverage, but does not report experimental benchmarks or quantitative results.
watch_item: Adoption may be difficult because the workflow depends on consistent interfaces and trustworthy statistical models across heterogeneous simulation and fabrication tools.
paper_title: SPICE-Q and Large-Scale Quantum Chip Production
